# 02 Hard copper porphyry

> What happens to recovery when the mill runs out of power?

A competent porphyry at a high work index; the installed ball-mill power binds and harder ore coarsens the grind.

| Case id | Category | Circuit family | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| `copper_porphyry_hard` | liberation | rougher | authored scenario; parameters inside cited ranges; not plant-calibrated |

Open it in the workbench: [https://oreflow.ml.fasl-work.com/?case=copper_porphyry_hard](https://oreflow.ml.fasl-work.com/?case=copper_porphyry_hard); on its own stage: [focus](https://oreflow.ml.fasl-work.com/focus/copper_porphyry_hard).

## The problem

The ball mill needs most of its installed power to reach the design grind at the design throughput. Any further hardness or tonnage cannot be met with more energy, so the grind coarsens until the power balance closes.

This is the most common way a concentrator loses recovery without any change in its flotation circuit, and the case is built to show that chain: power, then grind, then liberation, then recovery.

## The ore

| Mineral | Role | Mass fraction | Liberation size | Composite content | Host | Separation response |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chalcopyrite | Cu carrier (stoichiometric) | from the head grade | 100 µm | 0.35 | Quartz and silicate gangue | flotation |
| Pyrite | gangue | 0.025 | - | - | - | flotation |
| Quartz and silicate gangue | gangue | the balance | - | - | - | flotation |

| Payable | Head grade | Carried by |
|---|---|---|
| Cu | 0.520% | Chalcopyrite (100%, stoichiometric) |

Bond ball-mill work index 18.5 kWh/t; crushing work index 20.4 kWh/t.

## The operating point

The nominal state and the bounds Contract 1 allows for this case; the workbench validates every change against them.

| Input | Nominal | Allowed range |
|---|---|---|
| Ore throughput | 510 t/h | 255 t/h to 765 t/h |
| Grind target (P80) | 165 µm | 83 µm to 330 µm |
| Circulating load | 2.50 | 1.00 to 4.00 |
| Overflow water | 2.10 m³/t | 1.00 m³/t to 4.00 m³/t |
| Crusher closed-side setting | 8.00 mm | 4.00 mm to 16.00 mm |
| Bond work index | 18.5 kWh/t | 13.0 kWh/t to 27.8 kWh/t |
| Head grade | 0.52% | 0.26% to 0.78% |
| Collector dose | 25.0 g/t | 0.0 g/t to 75.0 g/t |
| Gas velocity (rougher) | 1.40 cm/s | 0.50 cm/s to 2.50 cm/s |
| Rougher cells | 8 | 3 to 12 |

## The six variants

Each variant changes exactly one input of the nominal state.

| Variant | Change | Recovery of the primary payable | Concentrate grade | Specific energy, total | Product P80 | Mill power | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nominal design | - | 92.3% | 23.72% | 16.18 kWh/t | 165 µm | 7,274 kW | - |
| Harder ore (+25% work index) | Bond work index: 18.5 kWh/t to 23.1 kWh/t (x1.25) | 83.7% | 22.84% | 16.70 kWh/t | 229 µm | 7,400 kW | `power_limited`, `cyclone_pressure` |
| Coarser grind target (+35% P80) | Grind target (P80): 165 µm to 223 µm (x1.35) | 84.9% | 23.19% | 13.66 kWh/t | 223 µm | 6,024 kW | `cyclone_pressure` |
| Higher throughput (+25%) | Ore throughput: 510 t/h to 638 t/h (x1.25) | 81.9% | 23.60% | 13.39 kWh/t | 229 µm | 7,400 kW | `power_limited`, `cyclone_pressure` |
| More collector (+60%) | Collector dose: 25.0 g/t to 40.0 g/t (x1.60) | 93.2% | 22.87% | 16.21 kWh/t | 165 µm | 7,274 kW | - |
| More air (+40% gas velocity) | Gas velocity (rougher): 1.40 cm/s to 1.96 cm/s (x1.40) | 93.3% | 23.79% | 16.25 kWh/t | 165 µm | 7,274 kW | - |

- **Harder ore (+25% work index).** Bond work index 25% higher. The circuit needs more energy per tonne for the same grind; where the installed power runs out the mill runs at its limit and the product coarsens, which then costs liberation.
- **Coarser grind target (+35% P80).** Grind target 35% coarser. Less energy per tonne and fewer liberated grains, so the concentrate grade falls; a flotation circuit pays for the energy saved in recovery as well, while magnetic drums keep capturing the coarser composites and recover a little more iron at the lower grade.
- **Higher throughput (+25%).** Throughput 25% higher. Once the mill reaches its installed power the grind coarsens, and in a flotation circuit the residence in every bank falls in proportion as well; the metal recovered per hour can still rise, because the extra tonnes outweigh the recovery lost.
- **More collector (+60%).** More collector. The valuable mineral's response saturates at a lower dose than the gangue's and the composites', so extra reagent adds recovery with diminishing returns and floats more of what dilutes the concentrate.
- **More air (+40% gas velocity).** Gas velocity 40% higher. A larger bubble surface area flux raises every rate constant; the froth also recovers more water, which carries more entrained gangue, but the faster flotation of the valuable mineral usually weighs more, so recovery rises and the grade holds or rises slightly.

## At the nominal state

| Check | Value | Plausible range | Within |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recovery of the primary payable | 92.3% | 82.0% to 93.0% | yes |
| Concentrate grade | 23.72% | 22.00% to 32.00% | yes |

Every unit and the circuit close within 1.1e-13 relative (the requirement is 1e-9). Water: 2.15 m³/t.

## Method records at the nominal state

- **Optimizer:** optimal at Grind target (P80) 161 µm, Collector dose 23.6 g/t, Gas velocity (rougher) 2.50 cm/s; active constraints: grade, power; recovered metal +2.01% against the nominal state (148 engine runs from 6 starts).
- **Uncertainty** (128 Latin-hypercube samples of the ore): recovery P05 84.9%, P50 91.5%, P95 93.8%; probability of meeting every constraint 29%.
- **Sobol indices** (1536 engine runs), the input with the largest total index: recovery of the primary payable: work index (total index 0.70); concentrate grade: liberation size (total index 0.79); specific energy, grinding: work index (total index 1.00); recovered primary payable: head grade (total index 0.94).
- **Kinetic fits:** of the five lumped models fitted to the virtual batch test, the gamma model projects the rougher bank closest to the exact bank recovery by true flotation (92.9%), 1.03 points below it.

## Scope and assumptions

The energy-specific population balance (Herbst and Fuerstenau 1980) scales breakage with power per tonne, so a power cap is a cap on breakage.

Installed power and every ore parameter are authored inside the recorded ranges; the case is not a specific plant.

## Reading it in the workbench

At the nominal state the mill already draws nearly all its installed power; in the harder-ore and higher-throughput variants the readout flags a power-limited state and the achieved P80 departs from the target.

Response: sweep throughput or work index and watch mill power reach the installed value and recovery turn down.

## Sources

- **breakage:** Moly-Cop Tools energy-specific selection (alpha0 0.0091 t/kWh, alpha1 0.651, alpha2 2.5, d_crit 6514 µm) and its documented alternative breakage set (beta0 0.4, beta1 0.65, beta2 4.02); dossier section 1.4.
- **crusher:** Whiten classification K1 0.5 to 0.95 CSS, K2 1.7 to 3.5 CSS, K3 about 2.3; dossier section 1.3.
- **cyclone:** Plitt geometry ratios typical of mineral-processing cyclones; sharpness and underflow density authored; dossier section 2.
- **flotation:** k from bubble surface area flux (Gorain et al. 1997), Savassi entrainment, perfect-mixer banks; floatability and widths authored within Trahar (1981) size behaviour; dossier section 3.
- **collector:** Saturating collector response with gangue saturating at higher dose (chalcopyrite/pyrite critical review, PMC9572913); dossier section 3.5.
- **water:** Process-water capacity per tonne of ore (pumping and thickener capacity), authored 5% above each case's nominal requirement; it is the water constraint of the operating-point optimizer.
- **kpi:** Nominal KPI ranges are typical practice ranges from the dossier section 3.7 and the cited sources; they are plausibility gates, not predictions.
